newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in thin late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in thin late trading.

text.p: Indonesia's rupiah was stable against the dollar in thin late trading on Wednesday amid ample liquidity, dealers said.

"Some small banks were seen buying rupiah to cover their position for year-end needs, but there was not much impact on the rupiah which is already hovering at the lower end of the central bank's fixing band," one local bank dealer said.
The dealer said the sufficient market liquidity also helped keep the rupiah spot rate stable despite some local buying.
Spot rupiah was last quoted at 2,353.90/54.00 against an opening of 2,353.50/54.50.
Dealers said earlier anticipation of an increase in the central bank's fixing rates had also kept the local currency stable despite the local rupiah buying.

Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,354/2,546 and the conversion band at 2,354/2,402 late on Wednesday as anticipated, in line with its current policy of raising the bands by three to four points per week.
One-month swap was at 16.00/16.50, two at 30.00/31.50, three at 43.50/45.00. Six-months swap was last at 87.00/88.00 points.
The foreign bank dealer said the spot rupiah rate was likely to range between 2,354.00 and 2,354.50 on Thursday.
Overnight swap was last at 0.45/0.55 from an opening of 0.50/0.60.
Tomorrow and today rupiah were last quoted at 2,353.00/53.45 and 2,353.50/54.50, respectively.
